rationale: Both menus in the Baroni study allowed potatoes and the separate ordinal OFF distributions were inconclusive. The Dresden study weighed cold potato salad during medicated ON visits, with consumption as the outcome. Low-protein diets varied whole meals, and the completed N-DOSE trial has no posted potato-to-OFF comparison. The direction for roasted potato and daily OFF time remains unresolved.

The original Khalid abstract confirms mania with celery root extract and concurrent drug and herb use. A secondary source calls the hallucinations visual, and the accessible original does not verify their modality or frequency. The dried-leaf thyroid case measured a different outcome. The direction for visual hallucination frequency after dried celery leaf in Parkinson disease remains unresolved.

A human trial measured anxiety in recipients of depleted Syrian oregano stems as a bay-leaf comparator without a no-oregano comparison. Dried oregano leaf infusion reduced mouse exploration alongside motor impairment, and extract studies report different behavior in different models. These findings give no defensible direction for dried oregano and Parkinson anxiety.
